Hold, breathing into the stretch through your right glute and the front of your left hip, then rise slowly and switch sides on another round.
exercises.caution: Skip or use a cushion under the front hip if you have knee pain — this is a deep hip-opener, not a beginner stretch.

exercises.name: Bridge Pose
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, close to your hips.
Press through your feet and lift your hips toward the ceiling, squeezing your glutes as you rise.
Clasp your hands underneath you and roll your shoulders in to open your chest, or keep arms flat by your sides.
Hold, feeling the stretch across your hip flexors and chest, then lower your spine back down slowly, one vertebra at a time.
exercises.caution: Skip if you have neck or lower-back issues — keep the neck neutral and avoid turning your head while lifted.

animationCallout.text: Press your hips up toward the ceiling

exercises.name: Standing Split Prep Stretch
instructions: Stand facing a wall or sturdy chair for balance and hinge forward from your hips, hands on the support.
Shift your weight onto your left leg and lift your right leg straight up behind you as high as comfortably possible.
Keep both legs as straight as you can and square your hips toward the floor.
Hold, feeling the stretch through the standing leg's hamstring, then lower slowly and switch sides on another round.
exercises.caution: Only lift as high as you can while keeping the standing leg straight and controlled — use a wall for balance.

animationCallout.text: Lift your back leg higher, straight behind you

exercises.name: Extended Exhale Breathing
instructions: Sit or lie down in a comfortable position and relax your shoulders.
Inhale gently through your nose for 4 counts.
Exhale slowly through your nose or pursed lips for 8 counts, twice as long as your inhale.
Repeat for the full duration, letting your body settle deeper with each exhale.

exercises.name: Counting Down Sleep Breath
instructions: Lie down in bed or a comfortable reclined position and close your eyes.
Inhale slowly through your nose, then exhale while silently counting 'ten.'
Inhale again, then exhale while counting 'nine,' continuing to count down with each exhale.
If you lose track, simply restart from ten — the goal is a slow, wandering mind, not a perfect count.

exercises.name: Cooling Sitali Breath
instructions: Sit comfortably and curl the sides of your tongue inward to form a tube, then stick it slightly past your lips.
Inhale slowly through the curled tongue, feeling a cool sensation on your tongue.
Close your mouth and exhale slowly through your nose.
Repeat for the full duration to help cool the body and calm the mind.
exercises.caution: If you can't curl your tongue, sip air through slightly parted, pursed lips instead.

exercises.name: Three-Part Breath (Dirga Pranayama)
instructions: Lie down or sit tall and place one hand on your belly and one on your chest.
Inhale slowly, filling your belly first, then your ribcage, then your upper chest.
Exhale slowly in reverse order, releasing your chest first, then ribs, then belly.
Continue this three-part wave of breath, moving slowly and smoothly for the full duration.

exercises.name: Body Scan Breathing
instructions: Lie down comfortably and take a few natural breaths to settle in.
With each inhale, bring your attention to a new part of your body, starting at your feet.
With each exhale, consciously relax that body part before moving your attention upward on the next inhale.
Continue scanning up through your legs, torso, arms, and head until the timer ends.

exercises.name: Segmented Exhale Breathing (Viloma)
instructions: Sit or lie down comfortably and take one full inhale through your nose.
Exhale slowly, but pause briefly two or three times partway through the exhale instead of releasing it all at once.
Resume the exhale after each pause until your lungs feel empty, then inhale normally.
Repeat the segmented exhale for the full duration.

exercises.name: Progressive Relaxation Breath
instructions: Lie down comfortably and take a slow breath in while gently tensing your feet and calves.
Exhale fully while releasing that tension completely, feeling the muscles go heavy.
Inhale again, tensing the next muscle group up (thighs, then glutes, then abs, and so on), and exhale to release.
Work your way up your whole body, pairing each tense-and-release with one slow breath cycle.

exercises.name: Left-Nostril Calming Breath (Chandra Bhedana)
instructions: Sit comfortably and bring your right hand up, folding your index and middle fingers into your palm.
Close your right nostril gently with your right thumb and inhale slowly through your left nostril only.
Close your left nostril with your ring finger, release your thumb, and exhale slowly through your right nostril.
Continue inhaling only through the left and exhaling only through the right for the full duration — this pattern is traditionally used to calm and cool the body before rest.

exercises.name: Standing IT Band Side Stretch (Left)
instructions: Stand tall next to a wall for balance and cross your left leg behind your right leg.
Reach your left arm overhead and lean your torso to the right, away from your left hip.
Push your left hip out to the side as you lean, feeling the stretch along the outside of your left thigh.
Hold, then return to center slowly and switch sides on another round.

animationCallout.text: Push your hip out to the side

exercises.name: Standing IT Band Side Stretch (Right)
instructions: Stand tall next to a wall for balance and cross your right leg behind your left leg.
Reach your right arm overhead and lean your torso to the left, away from your right hip.
Push your right hip out to the side as you lean, feeling the stretch along the outside of your right thigh.
Hold, then return to center slowly and switch sides on another round.

animationCallout.text: Push your hip out to the side

exercises.name: Dynamic Standing Leg Swings
instructions: Stand next to a wall or sturdy support and hold on lightly with one hand.
Swing your outside leg forward and backward in a smooth, controlled pendulum motion, keeping your knee soft.
Let the swing grow gradually taller as your hips loosen, without forcing the range of motion.
After the set time, turn around and repeat with the other leg.
exercises.caution: Keep the motion controlled, not kicking — this is a warm-up mobilizer, not a max-range stretch.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Circles
instructions: Stand with your hands on your hips, feet a little wider than shoulder-width apart.
Shift your hips in a slow, wide circle, first tracing several circles clockwise.
Keep your upper body relatively still and let the movement come from your hips.
Reverse direction and circle counter-clockwise for the remaining time.

animationCallout.text: Circle your hips in a wide loop

exercises.name: Runner's Lunge with Rotation (Left)
instructions: Step your left foot forward into a deep lunge, back leg straight and back heel lifted.
Place your right hand on the floor or a block inside your left foot for support.
Reach your left arm up toward the ceiling, rotating your chest open to the left.
Hold, feeling the stretch through your right hip flexor and your rotated torso, then release and switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Runner's Lunge with Rotation (Right)
instructions: Step your right foot forward into a deep lunge, back leg straight and back heel lifted.
Place your left hand on the floor or a block inside your right foot for support.
Reach your right arm up toward the ceiling, rotating your chest open to the right.
Hold, feeling the stretch through your left hip flexor and your rotated torso, then release and switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Standing Ankle Dorsiflexion Stretch (Left)
instructions: Stand facing a wall, about a foot away, with your left foot planted flat behind you.
Keeping your left heel on the ground, bend your left knee forward toward the wall.
Ease your knee forward until you feel a stretch through the front of your ankle and up your shin.
Hold, then release and switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Standing Ankle Dorsiflexion Stretch (Right)
instructions: Stand facing a wall, about a foot away, with your right foot planted flat behind you.
Keeping your right heel on the ground, bend your right knee forward toward the wall.
Ease your knee forward until you feel a stretch through the front of your ankle and up your shin.
Hold, then release and switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: 20-20-20 Focus Shift
instructions: Sit comfortably and look at something roughly 20 feet (6 metres) away.
Let your eyes settle on it without straining to focus.
Hold your gaze there for about 20 seconds, breathing slowly.
Blink softly a few times to refresh your eyes.
Return to your near task; repeat whenever your eyes feel tired.
exercises.caution: This is a rest break, not a treatment. See an eye professional for persistent eye pain or changes in vision.

exercises.name: Gentle Eye Rolls
instructions: Sit tall and keep your head still, looking straight ahead.
Slowly move your gaze up, then trace a smooth circle: up, right, down, left.
Keep the movement slow and comfortable — never forced.
Complete 3 to 4 slow circles, then reverse direction.
Blink and let your eyes rest for a moment when finished.
exercises.caution: Stop if you feel dizzy or any eye strain. Skip if you have a recent eye injury or eye condition.

exercises.name: Jaw-Open Temporalis Stretch
instructions: Sit or stand tall with relaxed shoulders.
Slowly open your mouth as wide as is comfortable and pain-free.
Feel a gentle stretch through the temples and jaw.
Hold for about 5 seconds, then slowly close.
Repeat gently and slowly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Keep within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop if your jaw clicks, locks, or hurts, and see a dentist for diagnosed TMJ problems.

exercises.name: Resisted Jaw Opening
instructions: Place your thumb or two fingers gently under your chin.
Slowly open your mouth against light resistance from your fingers.
Use only a small, gentle amount of pressure — this is not a strength test.
Open a short way, hold for 3 seconds, then slowly close.
Repeat calmly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Use very light resistance and stay pain-free. Stop if you feel clicking, locking, or pain, and see a dentist for diagnosed TMJ problems.

exercises.name: Side-to-Side Jaw Glide
instructions: Relax your jaw with your teeth slightly apart.
Slowly glide your lower jaw to one side as far as is comfortable.
Return to centre, then glide gently to the other side.
Keep the movement small, smooth, and pain-free.
Continue slowly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move gently within a comfortable range. Stop if the jaw clicks, locks, or hurts, and see a dentist for diagnosed TMJ problems.

exercises.name: Tongue-Up Controlled Open/Close
instructions: Rest the tip of your tongue lightly on the roof of your mouth, behind your front teeth.
Keeping the tongue there, slowly open your mouth only as far as it stays in contact.
This keeps the jaw opening controlled and centred.
Hold briefly, then slowly close.
Repeat calmly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Keep it slow and pain-free. Stop if you feel clicking, locking, or pain, and see a dentist for diagnosed TMJ problems.

exercises.name: Frontalis Release
instructions: Rest the pads of your fingers gently across your forehead.
Let your eyebrows relax downward as you breathe out slowly.
Apply light, still pressure — no rubbing or pulling on the skin.
Hold and breathe slowly, letting the forehead soften.
Release gently after the hold and repeat.
exercises.caution: Use light pressure only. Avoid if you have a skin condition or injury on the forehead.

exercises.name: Physiological Sigh (Double Inhale Exhale)
instructions: Sit or stand comfortably with your shoulders relaxed.
Inhale deeply through your nose until your lungs feel full.
Without exhaling, take a second short, sharp inhale to top off your lungs completely.
Exhale slowly and fully through your mouth, letting your shoulders and jaw release.
Pause briefly, then begin the next double inhale.
Repeat the double-inhale, long-exhale pattern for the full duration.

exercises.name: Resonant Frequency Breathing (6 Breaths per Minute)
instructions: Sit upright in a relaxed, supported position.
Inhale gently through your nose for a slow count of 5.
Exhale gently through your nose or mouth for a slow count of 5.
Keep the breath smooth and unforced — an even, unhurried rhythm matters more than precise counting.
Let your belly and chest rise and fall together naturally.
Continue the steady in-and-out rhythm for the full duration.
exercises.caution: If counting to 5 feels strained, shorten the count until the breath feels comfortable.

exercises.name: Right-Nostril Energizing Breath (Surya Bhedana)
instructions: Sit tall in a comfortable cross-legged or chair position.
Rest your left hand on your knee and bring your right hand toward your nose.
Close your left nostril with your ring finger and inhale slowly through your right nostril.
Close your right nostril with your thumb, release your left nostril, and exhale slowly through the left side.
Continue inhaling through the right nostril and exhaling through the left for the full duration.
Let your breath stay smooth and unforced throughout.
exercises.caution: Skip this practice if you have high blood pressure, feel anxious or overheated, or are practicing close to bedtime — it's energizing, not calming.

exercises.name: Skull Shining Breath (Kapalabhati)
instructions: Sit tall with a long spine and relaxed shoulders.
Take one slow, deep inhale to begin.
Sharply contract your lower belly to push a short, forceful exhale out through your nose.
Let the inhale that follows happen passively and naturally as your belly relaxes.
Continue the quick, rhythmic pumping exhales for about 20 pumps, then return to normal breathing and rest.
Repeat for one or two more rounds if comfortable, resting between each.
exercises.caution: Avoid if pregnant, or if you have high blood pressure, a hernia, or recent abdominal or eye surgery. Stop immediately if you feel lightheaded.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch (Left Lead Leg)
instructions: From standing, step your left foot forward into a deep lunge, extending your right leg straight behind you.
Place both hands on the floor inside your left foot to support your balance.
Drop your right hip toward the floor to deepen the stretch through the back leg's hip flexor.
Rotate your torso and reach your left arm toward the ceiling, opening your chest to the left.
Return your hand to the floor, then straighten your left leg to feel the stretch shift into the hamstring.
Bend the left knee again and repeat the reach-and-straighten cycle smoothly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move within a pain-free range and skip the torso rotation if you feel any low-back strain.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch (Right Lead Leg)
instructions: From standing, step your right foot forward into a deep lunge, extending your left leg straight behind you.
Place both hands on the floor inside your right foot to support your balance.
Drop your left hip toward the floor to deepen the stretch through the back leg's hip flexor.
Rotate your torso and reach your right arm toward the ceiling, opening your chest to the right.
Return your hand to the floor, then straighten your right leg to feel the stretch shift into the hamstring.
Bend the right knee again and repeat the reach-and-straighten cycle smoothly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move within a pain-free range and skip the torso rotation if you feel any low-back strain.

exercises.name: Seated Spinal Rotation with Overhead Reach (Left)
instructions: Sit tall on a chair or the floor with your feet grounded and spine long.
Reach your left arm straight overhead, lengthening the left side of your body.
Rest your right hand on your left knee or the chair for support.
Gently rotate your torso to the left, leading with your chest, while keeping the overhead reach.
Hold the rotation and reach, breathing slowly into the stretch along your side and back.
Release back to center with control.
exercises.caution: Rotate only as far as feels comfortable, and avoid forcing the twist if you have a back condition.

exercises.name: Seated Spinal Rotation with Overhead Reach (Right)
instructions: Sit tall on a chair or the floor with your feet grounded and spine long.
Reach your right arm straight overhead, lengthening the right side of your body.
Rest your left hand on your right knee or the chair for support.
Gently rotate your torso to the right, leading with your chest, while keeping the overhead reach.
Hold the rotation and reach, breathing slowly into the stretch along your side and back.
Release back to center with control.
exercises.caution: Rotate only as far as feels comfortable, and avoid forcing the twist if you have a back condition.

exercises.name: Standing Adductor Rock (Side-to-Side)
instructions: Stand with your feet spread wide apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Shift your weight onto your left leg, bending the left knee while keeping your right leg straight, feeling the stretch along the inner right thigh.
Rock your weight across to the right leg, bending the right knee while straightening the left leg.
Keep your chest lifted and hands resting on your thighs or hips for balance throughout.
Continue rocking smoothly side to side for the full duration.

exercises.name: Standing Tibialis Raise (Toe Lifts)
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, near a wall or chair for balance if needed.
Keeping your heels planted, lift the balls of your feet and toes up off the floor as high as you can.
Hold briefly at the top, feeling the engagement along the front of your shins.
Lower your toes back down with control.
Repeat the lift-and-lower rhythm for the full duration.

exercises.name: Thumb Extension Stretch (Left)
instructions: Hold your left hand up with fingers relaxed.
Use your right hand to gently bend your left thumb back and down, away from your palm.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the base of the thumb.
Release and repeat 2-3 times.

animationCallout.text: Bend your thumb back and down

exercises.name: Thumb Extension Stretch (Right)
instructions: Hold your right hand up with fingers relaxed.
Use your left hand to gently bend your right thumb back and down, away from your palm.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the base of the thumb.
Release and repeat 2-3 times.

animationCallout.text: Bend your thumb back and down

exercises.name: Hook Fist Tendon Glide
instructions: Hold both hands up in front of you with fingers straight.
Bend only your first and second knuckles to form a hook shape, keeping your knuckles at the base of the fingers straight.
Hold for 3-5 seconds, then straighten your fingers fully.
Repeat the hook-and-straighten motion for the full duration to glide the finger tendons.

animationCallout.text: Curl your fingertips into a hook, knuckles straight

exercises.name: Fist-to-Fan Tendon Gliding Flow
instructions: Start with both hands in loose, relaxed fists.
Slowly open your fingers and spread them as wide as you can, like a fan.
Hold the spread for 2-3 seconds, then curl back into a fist.
Repeat the fist-to-fan sequence slowly for the full duration.

animationCallout.text: Spread your fingers wide, then curl into a fist

exercises.name: Towel Scrunch (Toe Flexor Stretch)
instructions: Sit in a chair with a small towel laid flat on the floor under your feet.
Using only your toes, scrunch the towel toward you, gripping and pulling it inward.
Release and reset the towel flat, then repeat.
Continue scrunching for the full duration to work the small muscles under your feet.

animationCallout.text: Curl your toes to scrunch the towel toward you

exercises.name: Big Toe Extension Stretch (Left)
instructions: Sit and cross your left ankle over your right knee.
Use your hand to gently pull your left big toe upward and back toward your shin.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the sole and big toe.
Release and repeat 2-3 times.

animationCallout.text: Pull your big toe up toward your shin

exercises.name: Big Toe Extension Stretch (Right)
instructions: Sit and cross your right ankle over your left knee.
Use your hand to gently pull your right big toe upward and back toward your shin.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the sole and big toe.
Release and repeat 2-3 times.

animationCallout.text: Pull your big toe up toward your shin

exercises.name: Seated Toe-to-Shin Stretch (Left)
instructions: Sit toward the edge of a chair and extend your left leg with your heel on the floor.
Reach down and gently pull the ball of your left foot and toes back toward your shin.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch through the bottom of the foot and calf.
Release and repeat 2-3 times.

exercises.name: Seated Toe-to-Shin Stretch (Right)
instructions: Sit toward the edge of a chair and extend your right leg with your heel on the floor.
Reach down and gently pull the ball of your right foot and toes back toward your shin.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch through the bottom of the foot and calf.
Release and repeat 2-3 times.

exercises.name: Jaw Relaxation Drop
instructions: Sit or stand comfortably and let your shoulders relax.
Rest your tongue lightly on the roof of your mouth just behind your front teeth.
Let your lips stay gently closed while allowing your back teeth to come apart, letting your jaw hang loose.
Breathe slowly and hold this passive, relaxed position for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move gently within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop if your jaw clicks, locks, or hurts, and see a dentist for diagnosed TMJ problems.

exercises.name: Circular Temple Self-Massage
instructions: Place your fingertips lightly on your temples, just beside your eyebrows.
Make small, slow circular motions with light pressure.
Circle in one direction for half the time, then reverse direction.
Breathe slowly throughout to help release tension.
exercises.caution: Use gentle pressure only. Skip if you have a headache disorder that worsens with touch or any scalp or skin condition.

animationCallout.text: Massage your temples in small circles

exercises.name: Figure-8 Eye Tracking
instructions: Sit comfortably and hold your head still, facing forward.
Without moving your head, trace a slow, wide figure-8 shape in the air with your eyes.
Complete a few slow figure-8s in one direction, then reverse.
Keep the motion smooth and unhurried for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Stop if you feel dizzy or any eye strain. Skip if you have a recent eye injury or eye condition.

exercises.name: Full Scalp Massage (Tension Release)
instructions: Place your fingertips on your scalp, spread wide like a claw.
Press lightly and move your scalp in small circles over the skull, not just sliding over the hair.
Work slowly from your hairline back toward the crown and down toward the base of your skull.
Breathe slowly and keep the pressure light and comfortable throughout.
exercises.caution: Use gentle pressure only. Skip if you have a headache disorder that worsens with touch or any scalp or skin condition.

animationCallout.text: Massage your scalp in small circles

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Switch (Rotation Flow)
instructions: Sit on the floor with both knees bent, one leg in front of you and one out to the side, each at roughly 90 degrees.
Keeping your chest tall, lift both knees slightly and rotate them to switch sides, so the front leg becomes the side leg and vice versa.
Lower down into the new position with control.
Continue switching sides smoothly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move with control rather than momentum, and keep the motion pain-free through the hips and knees.

exercises.name: Shoulder Pendulum Swing (Left)
instructions: Lean forward slightly and support yourself with your right hand on a chair or table.
Let your left arm hang loose and relaxed toward the floor.
Gently swing the arm in small circles, letting gravity do the work rather than using muscle effort.
Continue the slow, passive swinging for the full duration, then switch sides on another round.

animationCallout.text: Let your arm hang and swing gently in circles

exercises.name: Shoulder Pendulum Swing (Right)
instructions: Lean forward slightly and support yourself with your left hand on a chair or table.
Let your right arm hang loose and relaxed toward the floor.
Gently swing the arm in small circles, letting gravity do the work rather than using muscle effort.
Continue the slow, passive swinging for the full duration, then switch sides on another round.

animationCallout.text: Let your arm hang and swing gently in circles

exercises.name: Standing Lumbar Side Glide (Lateral Shift)
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides.
Keeping your shoulders level and facing forward, shift your hips directly to one side without bending or twisting.
Hold briefly, feeling the stretch along one side of your lower back, then glide back to center.
Repeat, shifting to the other side, alternating for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move within a comfortable range and stop if you feel sharp or radiating pain.

animationCallout.text: Shift your hips directly to one side

exercises.name: Neck Isometric Front-and-Back Press
instructions: Sit or stand tall and place one palm flat against your forehead.
Gently press your head forward into your hand without letting your head actually move, holding for 5 seconds.
Release, then place a hand behind your head and gently press backward into it without moving your head, holding for 5 seconds.
Alternate front and back presses for the full duration, keeping the effort light.
exercises.caution: Use only gentle, pain-free pressure and stop if you feel dizziness or sharp pain.

animationCallout.text: Press your head into your hand without moving it

exercises.name: Seated Neck Half-Circles (Ear-to-Shoulder Arc)
instructions: Sit tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Slowly drop your chin toward your chest, then arc your head so your right ear moves toward your right shoulder.
Continue the slow arc back through center to bring your left ear toward your left shoulder.
Keep the motion in the front half only — avoid tilting your head backward — and repeat slowly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move gently and stop if you feel dizziness or sharp pain. Keep the arc in front, not tilting backward.

exercises.name: Table-Edge Bicep Stretch (Left)
instructions: Stand beside a sturdy table with your left arm straight and your palm flat on the table edge behind you, fingers pointing backward.
Keeping your arm straight, slowly turn your body away from the table.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the front of your upper arm.
Release and repeat 2-3 times, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Table-Edge Bicep Stretch (Right)
instructions: Stand beside a sturdy table with your right arm straight and your palm flat on the table edge behind you, fingers pointing backward.
Keeping your arm straight, slowly turn your body away from the table.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the front of your upper arm.
Release and repeat 2-3 times, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Standing Cross-Body Triceps Press (Left)
instructions: Reach your left arm across your chest, keeping it straight and at shoulder height.
Use your right forearm to press your left arm closer to your chest.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch through the back of the left upper arm and shoulder.
Release and repeat 2-3 times, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Standing Cross-Body Triceps Press (Right)
instructions: Reach your right arm across your chest, keeping it straight and at shoulder height.
Use your left forearm to press your right arm closer to your chest.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch through the back of the right upper arm and shoulder.
Release and repeat 2-3 times, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Seated Assisted Tibialis Stretch (Left)
instructions: Sit with your left ankle crossed over your right knee.
Use your hand to gently point your left foot and toes downward and away from your shin.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the front of the shin.
Release and repeat 2-3 times, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Seated Assisted Tibialis Stretch (Right)
instructions: Sit with your right ankle crossed over your left knee.
Use your hand to gently point your right foot and toes downward and away from your shin.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the front of the shin.
Release and repeat 2-3 times, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Active Shoulder Shrug & Release (Left)
instructions: Sit or stand tall with your arms relaxed at your sides.
Slowly raise your left shoulder up toward your left ear as far as comfortable.
Hold for 3-5 seconds, feeling the contraction, then let it drop and fully relax down.
Repeat the shrug-and-release for the full duration, then switch sides on another round.

animationCallout.text: Raise your shoulder up toward your ear

exercises.name: Active Shoulder Shrug & Release (Right)
instructions: Sit or stand tall with your arms relaxed at your sides.
Slowly raise your right shoulder up toward your right ear as far as comfortable.
Hold for 3-5 seconds, feeling the contraction, then let it drop and fully relax down.
Repeat the shrug-and-release for the full duration, then switch sides on another round.

animationCallout.text: Raise your shoulder up toward your ear

exercises.name: Grip and Release (Hand Squeeze Stretch)
instructions: Hold both hands out in front of you, relaxed.
Squeeze both hands into firm fists and hold for 3-5 seconds.
Release and spread your fingers wide open, holding for 3-5 seconds.
Repeat the squeeze-and-release cycle for the full duration.

animationCallout.text: Squeeze into a fist, then spread your fingers wide

exercises.name: Standing Waist Twist (Dynamic Rotation Flow)
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and knees soft, arms relaxed and swinging loosely.
Gently rotate your torso to one side, letting your arms swing naturally with the motion.
Rotate back through center and continue to the other side.
Keep the motion light and controlled, alternating sides for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Keep the twist gentle and controlled — this is a mobility warm-up, not a forceful stretch.

exercises.name: Wall Slide (Shoulder Blade Mobility)
instructions: Stand with your back flat against a wall and your arms raised to form a 'W' shape, elbows and wrists touching the wall.
Slowly slide your arms up the wall into a 'Y' shape, keeping your elbows and wrists in contact with the wall as long as possible.
Slide back down to the starting 'W' position with control.
Repeat the slide up and down slowly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Keep the motion pain-free and only slide as high as you can while keeping your arms touching the wall.

exercises.name: Triangle Breathing (3-3-3)
instructions: Sit comfortably with your back straight.
Inhale slowly through your nose for 3 counts.
Hold gently for 3 counts.
Exhale slowly through your nose or mouth for 3 counts.
Repeat the three-count cycle for the full duration.

exercises.name: So-Hum Mantra Breath
instructions: Sit comfortably with your eyes closed and your spine tall.
As you inhale slowly through your nose, silently say 'So' to yourself.
As you exhale slowly, silently say 'Hum' to yourself.
Let your breath set the pace rather than forcing it, continuing the silent 'So-Hum' for the full duration.

exercises.name: Breath Counting Meditation
instructions: Sit comfortably with your eyes closed or softly focused downward.
Breathe naturally, and silently count '1' at the end of your first exhale.
Continue counting up by one at the end of each exhale, up to 10.
When you reach 10, or if you lose track, simply start again at 1.

exercises.name: Segmented Inhale Breathing (Viloma 2)
instructions: Sit or lie down comfortably and exhale fully to start.
Inhale slowly, but pause briefly two or three times partway through the inhale instead of breathing in all at once.
Once your lungs feel full, exhale slowly and smoothly in one continuous breath.
Repeat the segmented inhale for the full duration.

exercises.name: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding Breath
instructions: Sit comfortably and take one slow breath in and out to settle.
Breathing slowly, silently notice 5 things you can see around you.
Continue breathing slowly as you notice 4 things you can hear, then 3 things you can feel touching your body.
Finish by noticing 2 things you can smell and 1 thing you can taste, keeping your breath slow and even throughout.
exercises.caution: This is a grounding technique for calm attention, not a treatment for anxiety or panic disorders — seek professional support if you need it.

exercises.name: Standing Doorway Bicep Stretch (Left)
instructions: Stand in an open doorway and place your left palm flat against the door frame, arm straight, thumb pointing up.
Slowly rotate your body away from the doorway until you feel a stretch along the front of your left upper arm.
Keep your left elbow straight and your shoulder relaxed away from your ear.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then release slowly.

exercises.name: Standing Doorway Bicep Stretch (Right)
instructions: Stand in an open doorway and place your right palm flat against the door frame, arm straight, thumb pointing up.
Slowly rotate your body away from the doorway until you feel a stretch along the front of your right upper arm.
Keep your right elbow straight and your shoulder relaxed away from your ear.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then release slowly.

exercises.name: Behind-Back Prayer Bicep Stretch
instructions: Stand tall and bring both arms behind your back, elbows straight.
Press your palms together behind your back in a reverse prayer position, fingers pointing up.
Gently lift your hands away from your lower back until you feel a stretch through both biceps and forearms.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing steadily.

exercises.name: Wall-Assisted Bicep Stretch (Left)
instructions: Stand with your left side to a wall, arm's length away.
Place your left palm flat on the wall behind you at shoulder height, fingers pointing backward.
Slowly turn your torso away from the wall until you feel the stretch along your left bicep.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides another time if desired.

exercises.name: Wall-Assisted Bicep Stretch (Right)
instructions: Stand with your right side to a wall, arm's length away.
Place your right palm flat on the wall behind you at shoulder height, fingers pointing backward.
Slowly turn your torso away from the wall until you feel the stretch along your right bicep.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides another time if desired.

exercises.name: Overhead Bicep Reach with Strap (Left)
instructions: Hold a towel or strap in your left hand and raise your left arm overhead.
Bend your left elbow and let the strap drape down your back, keeping a gentle grip.
Straighten your left elbow as far as comfortable, feeling the stretch through the front of your upper arm.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, keeping your shoulder relaxed.

exercises.name: Overhead Bicep Reach with Strap (Right)
instructions: Hold a towel or strap in your right hand and raise your right arm overhead.
Bend your right elbow and let the strap drape down your back, keeping a gentle grip.
Straighten your right elbow as far as comfortable, feeling the stretch through the front of your upper arm.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, keeping your shoulder relaxed.

exercises.name: Seated Bicep Stretch on Chair Edge
instructions: Sit near the front edge of a sturdy chair and place both palms on the seat behind your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Keeping your elbows straight, slowly slide your hips slightly forward until you feel a stretch through both biceps.
Lift your chest and keep your shoulders down and back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing evenly.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch with Strap (Left)
instructions: Raise your left arm overhead and bend the elbow so your left hand drops behind your neck.
Reach your right hand up your back and grasp a towel or strap held by your left hand for extra reach.
Gently pull down on the strap until you feel a stretch along the back of your left upper arm.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, keeping your neck relaxed.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch with Strap (Right)
instructions: Raise your right arm overhead and bend the elbow so your right hand drops behind your neck.
Reach your left hand up your back and grasp a towel or strap held by your right hand for extra reach.
Gently pull down on the strap until you feel a stretch along the back of your right upper arm.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, keeping your neck relaxed.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Triceps Pull at Wall (Left)
instructions: Stand facing a wall and raise your left arm across your chest at shoulder height, elbow bent.
Place your left forearm against the wall for light resistance.
Use your right hand to gently press your left elbow further across your body.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling the stretch through the back of your left arm and shoulder.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Triceps Pull at Wall (Right)
instructions: Stand facing a wall and raise your right arm across your chest at shoulder height, elbow bent.
Place your right forearm against the wall for light resistance.
Use your left hand to gently press your right elbow further across your body.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling the stretch through the back of your right arm and shoulder.

exercises.name: Behind-Head Bilateral Triceps Stretch
instructions: Sit or stand tall and raise both arms overhead.
Bend both elbows so your hands drop behind your head, fingers interlaced if comfortable.
Gently press your elbows back and slightly together, feeling both triceps lengthen.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, keeping your ribs down and core gently engaged.

exercises.name: Seated Triceps Stretch with Towel (Left)
instructions: Sit tall and hold one end of a towel in your left hand, raising that arm overhead and bending the elbow.
Reach your right hand behind your lower back and take hold of the towel's other end.
Gently walk your right hand up the towel to deepen the stretch through your left triceps.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then relax.

exercises.name: Seated Triceps Stretch with Towel (Right)
instructions: Sit tall and hold one end of a towel in your right hand, raising that arm overhead and bending the elbow.
Reach your left hand behind your lower back and take hold of the towel's other end.
Gently walk your left hand up the towel to deepen the stretch through your right triceps.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then relax.

exercises.name: Kneeling Triceps Stretch on Chair
instructions: Kneel in front of a chair or low bench and place both forearms on the seat, elbows bent.
Sit your hips back toward your heels while keeping your forearms in place.
Let your chest sink toward the floor, feeling a stretch through both triceps and shoulders.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Stretch on Stair Edge (Left)
instructions: Stand on a stair or sturdy step with the ball of your left foot on the edge, heel hanging off.
Hold a railing for balance and slowly lower your left heel below the level of the step.
Keep your left knee straight to target the calf, and stop before any pain in the Achilles.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then rise back to neutral.
exercises.caution: Hold a stable railing throughout - do not attempt without support.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Stretch on Stair Edge (Right)
instructions: Stand on a stair or sturdy step with the ball of your right foot on the edge, heel hanging off.
Hold a railing for balance and slowly lower your right heel below the level of the step.
Keep your right knee straight to target the calf, and stop before any pain in the Achilles.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then rise back to neutral.
exercises.caution: Hold a stable railing throughout - do not attempt without support.

exercises.name: Downward-Facing Dog Calf Pump
instructions: From hands and knees, tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back into an inverted V shape.
Bend one knee at a time, pressing the opposite heel gently toward the floor.
Alternate pedaling your feet, pressing each heel down for a couple of seconds at a time.
Continue the gentle pedaling motion for the full duration.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Stretch with Towel (Left)
instructions: Sit on the floor with your left leg extended straight in front of you.
Loop a towel or strap around the ball of your left foot, holding one end in each hand.
Keeping your knee straight, gently pull the towel to draw your toes back toward your shin.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling the stretch through your calf.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Stretch with Towel (Right)
instructions: Sit on the floor with your right leg extended straight in front of you.
Loop a towel or strap around the ball of your right foot, holding one end in each hand.
Keeping your knee straight, gently pull the towel to draw your toes back toward your shin.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling the stretch through your calf.

exercises.name: Wall Calf Stretch, Bent-Knee Soleus Focus (Left)
instructions: Stand facing a wall with your left foot a step behind your right.
Bend both knees slightly, keeping your left heel pressed into the floor.
Lean your hips toward the wall until you feel a stretch lower in your left calf, near the Achilles.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then release.

exercises.name: Wall Calf Stretch, Bent-Knee Soleus Focus (Right)
instructions: Stand facing a wall with your right foot a step behind your left.
Bend both knees slightly, keeping your right heel pressed into the floor.
Lean your hips toward the wall until you feel a stretch lower in your right calf, near the Achilles.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then release.

exercises.name: Kneeling Calf Stretch on Cushion (Left)
instructions: Kneel on a cushion with your left foot forward, knee bent at about 90 degrees, right knee resting on the cushion behind you.
Keeping your left heel flat on the floor, gently shift your weight forward over your left knee.
Hold when you feel a stretch through the back of your left lower leg.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then return to center.

exercises.name: Kneeling Calf Stretch on Cushion (Right)
instructions: Kneel on a cushion with your right foot forward, knee bent at about 90 degrees, left knee resting on the cushion behind you.
Keeping your right heel flat on the floor, gently shift your weight forward over your right knee.
Hold when you feel a stretch through the back of your right lower leg.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then return to center.

exercises.name: Standing Bilateral Calf Stretch on Incline Board
instructions: Stand with both feet on an incline board or a thick book, toes pointing up the slope, heels on the floor.
Keep both knees straight and your posture tall.
Lean your body slightly forward from the ankles until you feel both calves stretch evenly.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing steadily.

exercises.name: Kneeling Tibialis Stretch, Toes Tucked (Left)
instructions: Kneel on a cushioned surface with your left toes tucked under, top of the foot facing the floor.
Keep your right knee forward for balance and slowly sit your hips back toward your left heel.
Stop when you feel a stretch along the front of your left shin.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, then release.
exercises.caution: Move slowly and stop immediately if you feel any sharp pain in the ankle or shin.

exercises.name: Kneeling Tibialis Stretch, Toes Tucked (Right)
instructions: Kneel on a cushioned surface with your right toes tucked under, top of the foot facing the floor.
Keep your left knee forward for balance and slowly sit your hips back toward your right heel.
Stop when you feel a stretch along the front of your right shin.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, then release.
exercises.caution: Move slowly and stop immediately if you feel any sharp pain in the ankle or shin.

exercises.name: Seated Shin Stretch with Strap (Left)
instructions: Sit with your left leg extended and loop a strap around the top of your left foot.
Gently pull the strap to point your left toes away from you, deepening the ankle flex.
Feel the stretch along the front of your left shin, keeping the motion gentle.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, then release slowly.

exercises.name: Seated Shin Stretch with Strap (Right)
instructions: Sit with your right leg extended and loop a strap around the top of your right foot.
Gently pull the strap to point your right toes away from you, deepening the ankle flex.
Feel the stretch along the front of your right shin, keeping the motion gentle.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, then release slowly.

exercises.name: Standing Tibialis Stretch Against Wall
instructions: Stand an arm's length from a wall, resting your hands on it for balance.
Point both sets of toes and press the tops of your feet gently into the floor behind you, one at a time if needed for balance.
Feel a stretch along the front of your shins as your ankles point away from you.
Hold for 15-20 seconds per side, alternating through the full duration.

exercises.name: Ankle Circles for Tibialis Release (Left)
instructions: Sit with your left leg extended and lifted slightly off the floor.
Slowly circle your left ankle clockwise ten times, then counterclockwise ten times.
Keep the motion slow and controlled, moving through the full available range.
Continue the circles for the full duration to release tension along the shin.

exercises.name: Ankle Circles for Tibialis Release (Right)
instructions: Sit with your right leg extended and lifted slightly off the floor.
Slowly circle your right ankle clockwise ten times, then counterclockwise ten times.
Keep the motion slow and controlled, moving through the full available range.
Continue the circles for the full duration to release tension along the shin.

exercises.name: Cross-Legged Shin Pull (Left)
instructions: Sit cross-legged with your left ankle resting on your right knee.
Use your left hand to gently pull the top of your left foot toward your shin.
Feel a mild stretch along the front of your left lower leg.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, then switch the leg position.

exercises.name: Cross-Legged Shin Pull (Right)
instructions: Sit cross-legged with your right ankle resting on your left knee.
Use your right hand to gently pull the top of your right foot toward your shin.
Feel a mild stretch along the front of your right lower leg.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, then switch the leg position.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Stretch Against Wall (Left)
instructions: Stand facing away from a wall, one hand resting on it for balance.
Bend your left knee and grasp your left ankle behind you, drawing the heel toward your glutes.
Keep your knees close together and your hips level, without arching your lower back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then lower your foot with control.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Stretch Against Wall (Right)
instructions: Stand facing away from a wall, one hand resting on it for balance.
Bend your right knee and grasp your right ankle behind you, drawing the heel toward your glutes.
Keep your knees close together and your hips level, without arching your lower back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then lower your foot with control.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Quad Stretch with Strap (Left)
instructions: Lie on your right side with your legs stacked.
Loop a strap around your left ankle and bend the knee, gently drawing the heel toward your glutes with the strap.
Keep your hips stacked and avoid arching your lower back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then release slowly.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Quad Stretch with Strap (Right)
instructions: Lie on your left side with your legs stacked.
Loop a strap around your right ankle and bend the knee, gently drawing the heel toward your glutes with the strap.
Keep your hips stacked and avoid arching your lower back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then release slowly.

exercises.name: Kneeling Couch Stretch, Rear Foot Elevated (Left)
instructions: Kneel in front of a couch or low chair, resting the top of your left foot on the seat behind you.
Bring your right foot forward into a lunge position, keeping your torso upright.
Gently press your hips forward until you feel a deep stretch through the front of your left thigh.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, easing off if you feel any knee discomfort.
exercises.caution: Skip this stretch if you have knee pain - it places more load on the knee than a standing quad stretch.

exercises.name: Kneeling Couch Stretch, Rear Foot Elevated (Right)
instructions: Kneel in front of a couch or low chair, resting the top of your right foot on the seat behind you.
Bring your left foot forward into a lunge position, keeping your torso upright.
Gently press your hips forward until you feel a deep stretch through the front of your right thigh.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, easing off if you feel any knee discomfort.
exercises.caution: Skip this stretch if you have knee pain - it places more load on the knee than a standing quad stretch.

exercises.name: Prone Quad Stretch on Mat
instructions: Lie face down on a mat with your legs extended.
Bend both knees and reach back to hold both ankles, or use straps if you can't reach.
Gently draw both heels toward your glutes, keeping your hips pressed into the mat.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing steadily.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Stretch with Chair Support (Left)
instructions: Stand beside a chair, resting your right hand on the backrest for balance.
Bend your left knee, bringing your heel up behind you, and catch your ankle with your left hand.
Keep your standing leg soft and your torso tall, drawing the heel gently toward your glutes.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then lower with control.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Stretch with Chair Support (Right)
instructions: Stand beside a chair, resting your left hand on the backrest for balance.
Bend your right knee, bringing your heel up behind you, and catch your ankle with your right hand.
Keep your standing leg soft and your torso tall, drawing the heel gently toward your glutes.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then lower with control.

exercises.name: Overhead Lat Stretch at Doorframe (Left)
instructions: Stand beside a doorframe and reach your left arm up to hold the top of the frame.
Keeping your arm straight, lean your hips away from the doorframe to the right.
Feel the stretch travel down the side of your torso through your left lat.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides another time if desired.

exercises.name: Overhead Lat Stretch at Doorframe (Right)
instructions: Stand beside a doorframe and reach your right arm up to hold the top of the frame.
Keeping your arm straight, lean your hips away from the doorframe to the left.
Feel the stretch travel down the side of your torso through your right lat.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides another time if desired.

exercises.name: Side-Bend Lat Stretch with Chair (Left)
instructions: Sit sideways on a chair with your left hip closest to the backrest.
Raise your left arm overhead and reach it across to the right, letting your torso side-bend.
Hold onto the chair seat with your right hand for stability.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling the stretch along your left side body.

exercises.name: Side-Bend Lat Stretch with Chair (Right)
instructions: Sit sideways on a chair with your right hip closest to the backrest.
Raise your right arm overhead and reach it across to the left, letting your torso side-bend.
Hold onto the chair seat with your left hand for stability.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling the stretch along your right side body.

exercises.name: Kneeling Lat Stretch, Arms Extended
instructions: Kneel in front of a low table or bench and place both hands on it, arms extended.
Sit your hips back toward your heels while keeping your arms straight and reaching forward.
Let your chest melt toward the floor, feeling a stretch along both sides of your back.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply into your ribcage.

exercises.name: Seated Cross-Body Lat Reach (Left)
instructions: Sit tall on the floor or a chair and raise your left arm overhead.
Reach your left arm across and slightly down toward your right knee, side-bending your torso.
Keep your hips grounded and reach through your fingertips.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling the stretch along your left lat and side body.

exercises.name: Seated Cross-Body Lat Reach (Right)
instructions: Sit tall on the floor or a chair and raise your right arm overhead.
Reach your right arm across and slightly down toward your left knee, side-bending your torso.
Keep your hips grounded and reach through your fingertips.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling the stretch along your right lat and side body.

exercises.name: Hanging Lat Stretch on Bar or Ledge
instructions: Find a sturdy bar, ledge, or door top you can safely hang from with both hands.
Let your body hang with straight arms, relaxing your shoulders down away from your ears.
Allow your body weight to gently lengthen both lats and your upper back.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, keeping your grip secure throughout.
exercises.caution: Only attempt this if you can hang safely and comfortably support your body weight - step down immediately if you feel any shoulder strain.

exercises.name: Bhastrika (Bellows Breath)
instructions: Sit tall with a straight spine and relax your shoulders.
Take a few normal breaths to settle, then begin forceful, equal inhales and exhales through the nose, about one per second.
Keep the motion coming from your diaphragm, like a bellows pumping air in and out.
Do 10-15 rapid breaths, then return to slow, normal breathing and notice the effects.
Repeat the cycle 2-3 times over the full duration, resting between rounds.
exercises.caution: Skip if pregnant or if you have high blood pressure, heart conditions, or feel dizzy - stop immediately if lightheaded.

exercises.name: Sitkari Breath (Hissing Cooling Breath)
instructions: Sit comfortably and gently clench your teeth together with lips slightly parted.
Inhale slowly through the gaps in your teeth, making a soft hissing sound.
Close your mouth and exhale slowly and completely through your nose.
Repeat this inhale-through-teeth, exhale-through-nose cycle for the full duration, noticing a cooling sensation.

exercises.name: Buteyko Control Pause Breathing
instructions: Sit tall and breathe normally for a minute to settle.
After a normal, relaxed exhale, gently pinch your nose and pause your breath.
Hold only until you feel the first definite urge to breathe - do not strain or push past comfort.
Release your nose and resume calm, quiet breathing through the nose, breathing slightly less than usual.
Rest for a minute, then repeat the pause 2-3 more times over the full duration.
exercises.caution: This practice is about a gentle first urge to breathe, not a maximal breath-hold - never force or strain, and stop if you feel unwell.

exercises.name: Cyclic Sighing (Multi-Cycle Protocol)
instructions: Sit or lie down comfortably.
Inhale through your nose, then take a second, shorter sharp inhale on top of it to fully fill your lungs.
Exhale slowly and completely through your mouth, letting the exhale last twice as long as the inhale.
Repeat this double-inhale, long-exhale cycle continuously and evenly for the full duration.

exercises.name: Extended Kumbhaka Breath Retention
instructions: Sit tall with a relaxed, straight spine.
Inhale slowly and fully through your nose over 4 counts.
Gently hold the breath in for 8 counts, keeping your chest and throat soft, not clenched.
Exhale slowly and completely through your nose over 6 counts, then pause briefly before the next inhale.
Continue this inhale-hold-exhale rhythm for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Skip breath retention if pregnant or if you have high blood pressure, heart conditions, or a history of fainting.

exercises.name: Rectangle Breathing (4-2-6-2)
instructions: Sit comfortably with a tall, relaxed spine.
Inhale slowly through your nose for 4 counts.
Hold gently for 2 counts, then exhale slowly through your mouth for 6 counts.
Hold gently again for 2 counts before your next inhale.
Repeat this uneven rectangular rhythm for the full duration.

exercises.name: Whispered "Ha" Release Breath
instructions: Sit or stand comfortably and take a slow breath in through your nose.
As you exhale, softly whisper a long, breathy "haaaa" sound, letting your jaw and shoulders relax.
Let each exhale feel like a release of tension, without forcing the sound.
Continue the slow inhale and whispered-exhale cycle for the full duration.

exercises.name: 4-4-8 Extended Exhale Countdown Breath
instructions: Sit or lie down in a comfortable position.
Inhale through your nose for 4 counts, then gently hold for 4 counts.
Exhale slowly and completely through your mouth for 8 counts, letting your body settle.
Continue this pattern steadily for the full duration, keeping the exhale twice as long as the inhale.

exercises.name: Overhead Finger Interlace Stretch
instructions: Sit or stand tall and interlace your fingers together in front of you.
Turn your palms to face away from you and straighten your arms overhead.
Press your palms gently upward, feeling the stretch through your fingers, palms, and wrists.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing steadily.

animationCallout.text: Press your palms up toward the ceiling

exercises.name: Table-Supported Wrist Extensor Stretch
instructions: Kneel or sit in front of a table and place the backs of both hands flat on the surface, fingers pointing toward you.
Keep your elbows straight and gently lean your body weight back.
Feel the stretch along the top of your wrists and forearms.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, easing off if you feel any sharp pain.

animationCallout.text: Lean your body weight back

exercises.name: Rubber Band Finger Abduction Stretch
instructions: Loop a rubber band or hair tie around all five fingers of one hand near the fingertips.
Spread your fingers apart against the resistance of the band, then slowly release.
Repeat the spread-and-release motion for both hands for the full duration.
Keep the movement slow and controlled rather than forcing the spread.

animationCallout.text: Spread your fingers against the band's resistance

exercises.name: Assisted Wrist Flexion Stretch (Left)
instructions: Extend your left arm in front of you with your palm facing down.
Use your right hand to gently press the back of your left hand downward, bending the wrist.
Keep your left elbow straight and feel the stretch along the top of your forearm and wrist.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then release slowly.

animationCallout.text: Press the back of your hand down

exercises.name: Assisted Wrist Flexion Stretch (Right)
instructions: Extend your right arm in front of you with your palm facing down.
Use your left hand to gently press the back of your right hand downward, bending the wrist.
Keep your right elbow straight and feel the stretch along the top of your forearm and wrist.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then release slowly.

animationCallout.text: Press the back of your hand down

exercises.name: Assisted Wrist Extension Stretch (Left)
instructions: Extend your left arm in front of you with your palm facing up.
Use your right hand to gently curl your left fingers back toward your body.
Keep your left elbow straight and feel the stretch along the underside of your forearm and wrist.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then release slowly.

animationCallout.text: Curl your fingers back toward your body

exercises.name: Assisted Wrist Extension Stretch (Right)
instructions: Extend your right arm in front of you with your palm facing up.
Use your left hand to gently curl your right fingers back toward your body.
Keep your right elbow straight and feel the stretch along the underside of your forearm and wrist.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then release slowly.

animationCallout.text: Curl your fingers back toward your body

exercises.name: Seated Foot Flex-and-Point Flow
instructions: Sit on the floor or a chair with your legs extended in front of you.
Flex both feet, pulling your toes back toward your shins.
Point both feet, reaching your toes away from you.
Continue alternating flex and point slowly for the full duration.

exercises.name: Standing Toe Curl Towel Grip (Both Feet)
instructions: Stand with a small towel laid flat on the floor in front of you, one foot on it at a time.
Scrunch your toes to gather the towel toward you, then relax and reset.
Repeat the scrunch-and-release with each foot for the full duration.
Keep your weight balanced and movements slow and controlled.

animationCallout.text: Curl your toes to gather the towel

exercises.name: Cross-Legged Foot Massage & Arch Stretch
instructions: Sit cross-legged and rest one ankle across the opposite knee.
Use your thumbs to press and knead along the arch of the raised foot.
Gently pull the toes back with your hand to add a light arch stretch.
Switch feet halfway through and repeat for the full duration.

animationCallout.text: Knead the arch and pull your toes back

exercises.name: Wall-Assisted Toe Extension Stretch (Left)
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place the toes of your left foot up against it, heel on the floor.
Keep your left leg mostly straight and lean your weight gently forward.
Feel the stretch along the bottom of your left foot and toes.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

animationCallout.text: Press your toes up against the wall

exercises.name: Wall-Assisted Toe Extension Stretch (Right)
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place the toes of your right foot up against it, heel on the floor.
Keep your right leg mostly straight and lean your weight gently forward.
Feel the stretch along the bottom of your right foot and toes.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

animationCallout.text: Press your toes up against the wall

exercises.name: Kneeling Arch Stretch, Toes Curled Under (Left)
instructions: Kneel on a cushioned surface with your toes curled under, left foot leading.
Slowly sit back toward your left heel, keeping the toes tucked.
Feel the stretch along the sole and toes of your left foot.
Hold for 15-25 seconds, easing off if the stretch feels too intense.
exercises.caution: Ease off immediately if you feel sharp pain in the toes or arch.

animationCallout.text: Sit back toward your heel

exercises.name: Kneeling Arch Stretch, Toes Curled Under (Right)
instructions: Kneel on a cushioned surface with your toes curled under, right foot leading.
Slowly sit back toward your right heel, keeping the toes tucked.
Feel the stretch along the sole and toes of your right foot.
Hold for 15-25 seconds, easing off if the stretch feels too intense.
exercises.caution: Ease off immediately if you feel sharp pain in the toes or arch.

animationCallout.text: Sit back toward your heel

exercises.name: Doorway Side Stretch with Overhead Reach (Left)
instructions: Stand sideways next to a doorway with your left side closest to the frame.
Raise your left arm overhead and grip the top of the door frame.
Lean your hips away from the doorway to the right, lengthening your left side.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Doorway Side Stretch with Overhead Reach (Right)
instructions: Stand sideways next to a doorway with your right side closest to the frame.
Raise your right arm overhead and grip the top of the door frame.
Lean your hips away from the doorway to the left, lengthening your right side.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Chair-Assisted Side Bend Stretch (Left)
instructions: Sit tall on the edge of a chair with your feet flat on the floor.
Raise your left arm overhead and hold the side of the chair seat with your right hand.
Bend gently to the right, reaching your left arm up and over.
Hold for 15-25 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Chair-Assisted Side Bend Stretch (Right)
instructions: Sit tall on the edge of a chair with your feet flat on the floor.
Raise your right arm overhead and hold the side of the chair seat with your left hand.
Bend gently to the left, reaching your right arm up and over.
Hold for 15-25 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Standing Windmill Side Reach Flow
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and arms out to the sides.
Reach your right hand down toward your left foot while your left arm reaches up, hinging at the hips.
Return to standing, then reach your left hand down toward your right foot.
Continue alternating sides slowly for the full duration.

exercises.name: Supine Side-to-Side Knee Drop (Dynamic Oblique Flow)
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and arms out to the sides for stability.
Slowly lower both knees to the right, keeping your shoulders on the floor.
Bring your knees back to center, then lower them to the left.
Continue alternating side to side gently for the full duration.

exercises.name: Standing Broom-Stick Rotation (Torso Twist with Prop)
instructions: Hold a broomstick, towel, or similar light prop across the back of your shoulders.
Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart and gently rotate your torso to the right.
Return to center, then rotate to the left.
Continue alternating slowly and with control for the full duration.

exercises.name: Kneeling Cat-Cow Side Bend (Lateral Flow)
instructions: Start on your hands and knees in a tabletop position.
Shift your hips and rib cage to the right, looking back toward your right hip.
Return to center, then shift to the left, looking back toward your left hip.
Continue alternating sides slowly for the full duration.

exercises.name: Reclined Figure-Four Stretch with Strap (Left)
instructions: Lie on your back and cross your left ankle over your right knee.
Loop a strap or towel around the back of your right thigh and hold both ends.
Gently pull your right thigh toward your chest, keeping your left knee open.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Reclined Figure-Four Stretch with Strap (Right)
instructions: Lie on your back and cross your right ankle over your left knee.
Loop a strap or towel around the back of your left thigh and hold both ends.
Gently pull your left thigh toward your chest, keeping your right knee open.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Standing Glute Stretch Against Wall (Left)
instructions: Stand an arm's length from a wall and place your left foot flat against it behind you, knee bent.
Keep your right leg supporting your weight and your hips square to the wall.
Gently push your left hip forward to deepen the stretch through the left glute.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
exercises.caution: Skip this if you have trouble balancing on one leg; try a seated variation instead.

exercises.name: Standing Glute Stretch Against Wall (Right)
instructions: Stand an arm's length from a wall and place your right foot flat against it behind you, knee bent.
Keep your left leg supporting your weight and your hips square to the wall.
Gently push your right hip forward to deepen the stretch through the right glute.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
exercises.caution: Skip this if you have trouble balancing on one leg; try a seated variation instead.

exercises.name: Seated Cross-Ankle Glute Stretch (Left)
instructions: Sit tall in a chair and cross your left ankle over your right knee.
Keep your left foot flexed to protect the knee.
Hinge forward slightly from your hips, keeping your back flat.
Hold for 15-25 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Seated Cross-Ankle Glute Stretch (Right)
instructions: Sit tall in a chair and cross your right ankle over your left knee.
Keep your right foot flexed to protect the knee.
Hinge forward slightly from your hips, keeping your back flat.
Hold for 15-25 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Deep Squat Hold (Glute & Hip Opener)
instructions: Stand with your feet slightly wider than hip-width, toes turned out slightly.
Lower into a deep squat, keeping your heels on the floor if possible.
Rest your elbows against the inside of your knees, pressing them gently outward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, keeping your chest lifted.
exercises.caution: Use a wall or chair for support if you have balance or knee concerns.

exercises.name: Frog Rock (Kneeling Glute Mobility Flow)
instructions: Start on your hands and knees, then widen your knees out to the sides as far as comfortable.
Turn your toes outward and keep your ankles in line with your knees.
Slowly rock your hips backward toward your heels, then forward again.
Continue the gentle rocking motion for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move gently and stop if you feel any pinching in the hips or groin.

animationCallout.text: Rock your hips back toward your heels, then forward

exercises.name: Supine Cross-Body Double Knee Pull (Bilateral Glute Release)
instructions: Lie on your back and hug both knees toward your chest.
Gently rock your knees in a small circular motion, keeping your lower back relaxed.
Pull your knees slightly closer with each breath out.
Hold and continue the gentle motion for the full duration.

exercises.name: Kneeling Side Lunge Adductor Stretch on Cushion (Left)
instructions: Kneel on a cushion or mat with your right knee down and your left leg extended out to the side.
Keep your left foot flat on the floor, toes pointing forward.
Shift your hips toward your right knee, feeling the stretch along your left inner thigh.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Kneeling Side Lunge Adductor Stretch on Cushion (Right)
instructions: Kneel on a cushion or mat with your left knee down and your right leg extended out to the side.
Keep your right foot flat on the floor, toes pointing forward.
Shift your hips toward your left knee, feeling the stretch along your right inner thigh.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Standing Adductor Stretch with Chair Support (Left)
instructions: Stand beside a chair and place your left foot up on the seat, leg extended out to the side.
Keep your right leg straight and your hips facing forward.
Bend your right knee slightly and lower your hips to deepen the stretch along your left inner thigh.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
exercises.caution: Use a sturdy, stable chair and hold onto something nearby for balance if needed.

exercises.name: Standing Adductor Stretch with Chair Support (Right)
instructions: Stand beside a chair and place your right foot up on the seat, leg extended out to the side.
Keep your left leg straight and your hips facing forward.
Bend your left knee slightly and lower your hips to deepen the stretch along your right inner thigh.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
exercises.caution: Use a sturdy, stable chair and hold onto something nearby for balance if needed.

exercises.name: Seated Wide-Leg Forward Reach (Straddle Stretch)
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended wide into a straddle position.
Keep your knees and toes pointing up toward the ceiling.
Hinge forward from your hips, reaching your hands out in front of you.
Hold for 25-40 seconds, keeping your back as straight as comfortable.

exercises.name: Supine Butterfly with Wall Support (Gravity Groin Release)
instructions: Lie on your back close to a wall and bring the soles of your feet together, knees bent.
Let your knees fall open toward the floor, using gravity to deepen the stretch.
Rest your arms at your sides and breathe slowly, letting your hips relax.
Hold for 45-60 seconds.

exercises.name: Standing Sumo Squat Hold (Adductor Opener)
instructions: Stand with your feet wide apart and toes turned out at about 45 degrees.
Lower into a squat, keeping your knees tracking over your toes.
Rest your hands on your thighs and gently press your knees outward.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, keeping your chest lifted.

exercises.name: Wall-Assisted Ear-to-Shoulder Stretch (Left)
instructions: Stand with your right shoulder lightly touching a wall.
Tilt your head to the left, bringing your left ear toward your left shoulder.
Use the wall as a reference to keep your right shoulder from hiking up.
Hold for 15-25 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Wall-Assisted Ear-to-Shoulder Stretch (Right)
instructions: Stand with your left shoulder lightly touching a wall.
Tilt your head to the right, bringing your right ear toward your right shoulder.
Use the wall as a reference to keep your left shoulder from hiking up.
Hold for 15-25 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Doorway Neck Release Stretch (Left)
instructions: Stand in a doorway and place your left hand on the door frame near hip height.
Gently pull your left shoulder down and away from your ear.
Tilt your head to the right and slightly forward to lengthen the left side of your neck.
Hold for 15-25 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Doorway Neck Release Stretch (Right)
instructions: Stand in a doorway and place your right hand on the door frame near hip height.
Gently pull your right shoulder down and away from your ear.
Tilt your head to the left and slightly forward to lengthen the right side of your neck.
Hold for 15-25 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Standing Shoulder Blade Squeeze (Scapular Retraction Flow)
instructions: Stand or sit tall with your arms relaxed at your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and slightly down, holding for 2-3 seconds.
Release and let your shoulders relax fully.
Repeat the squeeze-and-release for the full duration.

animationCallout.text: Squeeze your shoulder blades together

exercises.name: Prone Y-T-W Raise (Upper Back Activation Flow)
instructions: Lie face down with your arms extended overhead in a Y shape, thumbs pointing up.
Lift your arms slightly and hold briefly, then lower.
Move your arms out to a T shape and repeat the lift, then bend elbows into a W shape and repeat.
Cycle slowly through Y, T, and W positions for the full duration.

animationCallout.text: Lift your arms slightly off the floor

exercises.name: Seated Chair Neck Traction Stretch (Both Sides)
instructions: Sit tall in a chair and hold the underside of the seat with both hands.
Tilt your head gently to the right, then slowly to the left, pausing briefly on each side.
Keep your shoulders anchored down as your head moves.
Continue alternating sides slowly for the full duration.

exercises.name: Standing Wall Angels (Trapezius Mobility Flow)
instructions: Stand with your back, head, and arms against a wall, elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Slowly slide your arms up the wall as far as comfortable, keeping contact with the wall.
Slide your arms back down to the starting position.
Repeat the slow up-and-down motion for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Keep the range small if your arms or shoulders can't stay in contact with the wall comfortably.

exercises.name: Standing Overhead Reach Back Bend
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and raise both arms overhead.
Gently arch your upper back, looking slightly upward.
Keep your core lightly engaged to protect your lower back.
Hold for 15-25 seconds, then return to standing slowly.
exercises.caution: Keep the arch gentle and stop if you feel any lower-back discomfort.

exercises.name: Seated Chair Backbend (Supported Extension)
instructions: Sit toward the front edge of a sturdy chair with a backrest.
Walk your hands down toward the sides of the chair as you lean back over the top of the backrest.
Let your chest open and head relax back if comfortable.
Hold for 15-25 seconds, then slowly return upright.
exercises.caution: Use a stable chair and stop immediately if you feel dizzy or strain in your lower back.

exercises.name: Locust Pose (Prone Chest and Ab Lift)
instructions: Lie face down with your arms alongside your body, palms down.
Lift your chest, arms, and legs slightly off the floor at the same time.
Keep your neck long and gaze slightly forward.
Hold for 10-20 seconds, then lower back down slowly.
exercises.caution: Skip this if you have a lower-back injury; keep the lift small and pain-free.

exercises.name: Standing Side-to-Side Reach Extension Flow
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and interlace your fingers overhead.
Gently arch back slightly while reaching upward, then return to neutral.
Continue the gentle reach-and-return motion slowly for the full duration.
Keep your breathing steady throughout.

exercises.name: Kneeling Camel Prep (Supported Backbend)
instructions: Kneel on a cushioned surface with your hips stacked over your knees.
Place your hands on your lower back for support, fingers pointing down.
Gently lean your hips forward and arch your upper back, opening your chest.
Hold for 15-25 seconds, then return upright slowly.
exercises.caution: Move slowly and stop if you feel any strain in your lower back or knees.

exercises.name: Supine Pelvic Rock (Gentle Ab Mobilizer)
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Gently arch your lower back, lifting your belly slightly, then flatten it back into the floor.
Continue alternating the gentle arch and flatten motion slowly.
Repeat for the full duration, keeping the movement small and controlled.

exercises.name: Natural Breath Awareness (Anapana Meditation)
instructions: Sit comfortably with your eyes closed or softly focused downward.
Bring your attention to the natural sensation of air moving in and out of your nostrils.
Don't change your breath in any way -- simply observe its natural rhythm and depth.
Whenever your mind wanders, gently bring your attention back to the breath.
Continue this quiet observation for the full duration.

exercises.name: Wave Breath (Sequential Full-Body Breath)
instructions: Lie down or sit comfortably with one hand on your belly and one on your chest.
Inhale by filling your belly first, then your ribs, then your upper chest, like a rising wave.
Exhale in the reverse order: release your chest first, then your ribs, then your belly.
Let the motion feel continuous and fluid rather than three separate steps.
Continue the wave-like breathing for the full duration.

exercises.name: Yogic Ratio Breath (1:4:2 Pranayama)
instructions: Sit comfortably with a tall spine and relax your shoulders.
Inhale through your nose for 3 counts.
Gently hold the breath in for 12 counts, without straining.
Exhale slowly through your nose for 6 counts.
Repeat this 1:4:2 ratio for the full duration, shortening the hold anytime it feels forced.
exercises.caution: Never force the retention -- if you feel light-headed or strained, return to normal breathing. Avoid this technique if pregnant or if you have high or low blood pressure.

exercises.name: Abdominal Lock Breath (Uddiyana Bandha Prep)
instructions: Stand or sit with a tall spine and exhale completely through your mouth.
With your lungs empty, gently draw your belly in and up underneath your rib cage without inhaling.
Hold the lock briefly and comfortably, then release your belly and let air flow back in naturally.
Rest for a few normal breaths before repeating.
Continue this cycle for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Practice only on an empty stomach. Avoid if pregnant or menstruating, or if you have high or low blood pressure, glaucoma, a hernia, or ulcers. Stop if you feel dizzy.

exercises.name: Cadence Walking Breath (Step-Synced Breathing)
instructions: While walking at a comfortable pace, notice how many steps it takes to complete one inhale.
Inhale through your nose for about 3-4 steps.
Exhale through your nose or mouth for the same or slightly longer count of steps.
Keep the rhythm steady, adjusting the count to match your natural stride.
Continue syncing your breath to your steps for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Stay aware of your surroundings and only practice this while walking somewhere safe and familiar.

exercises.name: Voluntary Yawn Release Breath
instructions: Sit or stand comfortably and open your mouth wide as if beginning a yawn.
Inhale deeply through your open mouth, encouraging a full, genuine yawn if one arises.
Exhale with a long, relaxed sigh, letting your jaw and face go loose.
Repeat several deliberate yawn-breaths, letting your eyes water or shoulders drop if that happens naturally.
Continue for the full duration, resting between yawns as needed.

exercises.name: Breath of Gratitude (Affective Labeling Breath)
instructions: Sit comfortably and bring to mind one thing you feel grateful for.
Inhale slowly while silently naming that thing to yourself.
Exhale slowly, letting go of any tension in your body.
Choose a new thing to feel grateful for every few breaths, or stay with the same one.
Continue for the full duration.

exercises.name: Descending Ladder Breath (Step-Down Countdown)
instructions: Sit comfortably with a tall spine.
Inhale and exhale with an equal count of 6 seconds each.
On the next cycle, shorten both the inhale and exhale to 5 seconds, then 4, then 3, then 2, then 1.
Once you reach a count of 1, start again from 6 and repeat the countdown.
Continue the descending pattern for the full duration, keeping each breath smooth rather than rushed.
exercises.caution: If any count feels too fast or short of breath, stay at a longer count instead of continuing to descend.
